obligations.note: POST /payees/{id}/reopen is bound to privileged action manage_payees with mfa=False, so app.py does not require MFA. The exhaustive control test fails on that route, and EXC-0249 is limited to the reconciliation batch account while the route skips MFA for every caller.
reopen_payee only updates status and closed_at. It does not persist NPI, and test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed on the head commit.
reopen_payee authorizes manage_payees and records an audit event with actor, action reopen_payee, target payee id, and the clock time. The sampled audit control test passed.
The new UPDATE is a fixed SQL string with the payee id bound as a parameter. test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passed on the head commit.
Ticket CHG-24606 is standard, approved by change manager Erik Brandt before review, and its components cover payments.http, routes, service, and store.
Sofia Santos, a payments change approver and not the author, approved a code review of the head commit.
The change is a single commit, f763745, and both approvals name that commit.
CI on the final commit reports result failure: test_privileged_routes_require_mfa failed, so the payments suite did not pass.
The change touches security-sensitive http, routes, and store. Ines Halvorsen, a security reviewer, approved a security review of the head commit.

EXC-0249 is approved by a risk owner, unexpired, and names MFA-1 and payments.routes, but its scope is only the reconciliation batch account. The code waives MFA for the route generally, so the exception is out of scope and does not authorize the deviation.
Acceptance record ACR-0404 covered routes.py for MFA-1 and lapses because this commit changes route behavior. The replacement exhaustive control test on the head commit failed.

summary: The change adds POST /payees/{id}/reopen for privileged action manage_payees without MFA. That violates MFA-1, the cited exception does not cover a general waiver, and the exhaustive route control test fails on the final commit, so testing and lapsed-evidence requirements are also unmet. Audit, encryption at rest, and parameterized SQL for the new payee update are in order, and the ticket, independent code review, and security review match this single commit. The change is rejected.
